Construe

/kuhn-STROO/ - rhymes with true · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Construe means to interpret the meaning of something.

The neighbors construed the half-finished fence as a property claim, though the builder had simply run out of lumber.

Worked Example

When the composer marked the finale only “with fire,” every conductor construed the phrase differently: one took it as speed, another as fury, a third as brightness — three performances grown from the same two words.

Construe is more exact than interpret because the puzzle is the meaning of particular words — ambiguous ones, read closely and defensibly, often as one thing or another. And mind the sound-alike trap: construe means to read meaning out of something, while construct means to build; the two share a Latin root and little else today.

How Construe Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

interpret

interpret: the plain, neutral word for making sense of something

decode

decode: works out meaning that was deliberately hidden

Antonyms

overlook

overlook: to pass by without taking any meaning at all

garble

garble: to scramble a message instead of drawing sense from it

How Strong Is It? — read → construe → decipher

read vs. construe

read vs. construe: To read a note is lighter than to construe it — reading takes the words in, while construing works out what they are really meant to do.

decipher vs. construe

decipher vs. construe: Decipher goes further than construe: construing untangles ambiguous meaning, but deciphering cracks meaning that is hidden or garbled on purpose.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — strue

Root — strue: to pile up, to build (Latin struere)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + strue (to build, Latin struere) = to build the pieces of a sentence together — which is how Roman schoolboys used the word, assembling a Latin sentence's parts until its meaning stood up. Construe kept the meaning-building; its cousin construct kept the bricks.

Use the root in a new word: instruct

Use the root in a new word: instruct: A laminated card instructs new lifeguards on the tower's whistle signals.

Word Choice

formal / legal

Construe is precise where interpret is broad: it suits the careful, often disputed reading of particular words or acts, and it usually appears in the frame “construe something as something.” Contextualize, its neighbor in this unit, does different work — it supplies the surroundings; construe extracts the meaning.
